strings.name: Gordon Brown
strings.role: Public advocate · former UK prime minister and chancellor
strings.summary: Brown moved from history and Labour politics to the Treasury, serving as chancellor from 1997 to 2007 and advancing Bank of England operational independence and international debt relief. Prime minister from 2007 to 2010, he led Britain through the financial crisis and hosted the London G 20 summit. He later worked on education, child poverty and health financing, becoming the prime minister’s special reviewer on global finance and cooperation in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A former UK prime minister and chancellor who played a role in responding to the global financial crisis and advancing international education and development initiatives.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Giffnock, near Glasgow, Scotland, United Kingdom.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied history and earned a doctorate at Edinburgh; early work included teaching and television journalism.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Responding to financial crisis
strings.highlights.h1.text: As prime minister advanced bank support and hosted the 2009 London G 20 summit to coordinate international responses.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Education and health financing
strings.highlights.h2.text: After office, served as UN special envoy for global education and WHO ambassador for global health financing.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Appointed special reviewer
strings.timeline.t1.text: The UK government appointed him to review global finance and cooperation for the prime minister.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Became WHO financing ambassador
strings.timeline.t2.text: Appointed to advocate sustained health investment and equitable access to vaccines and care.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became UN education envoy
strings.timeline.t3.text: Focused on global education and access for children out of school.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Left the premiership
strings.timeline.t4.text: Unable to form a government after the election, left Downing Street; remained an MP until 2015.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Hosted London G 20 summit
strings.timeline.t5.text: World leaders pledged additional international financial resources and stronger financial regulation.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Advanced bank support
strings.timeline.t6.text: His government introduced bank recapitalization and guarantees; their effects and costs remain subjects of assessment.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Became prime minister
strings.timeline.t7.text: Succeeded Tony Blair and faced the global financial crisis and recession.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Became chancellor
strings.timeline.t8.text: Led the Treasury under Blair and announced operational independence for Bank of England interest-rate decisions.
strings.timeline.t9.title: First elected to Parliament
strings.timeline.t9.text: Elected for Dunfermline East, beginning more than three decades in Parliament.
